title: Split ephemeral network resources into transient state to reduce Terraform plan churn
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We routinely see noisy terraform plans for networking stacks during routine autoscaling and maintenance. Ephemeral artifacts created by autoscaling (elastic IP temp allocations, transient ENIs and short-lived route table associations) live in the same state as long-lived network foundations (VPCs, subnets, routing, security controls). That coupling causes plan churn, long apply times, and frequent race conditions when teams run parallel workstreams.

Goal: Refactor the networking IaC so that ephemeral, autoscaling-related resources are managed out-of-band in a separate transient state and workspace. This reduces plan surface for the long-lived network modules, speeds up applies, and minimizes accidental drift. We must keep operational semantics (cleanup, dependency guarantees) intact and preserve the ability to reconstruct resources from code.

Scope:
- Introduce a new terraform workspace and state namespace for transient networking resources (ephemeral EIPs, autoscale ENIs, NAT gateway ephemeral allocations, instance-specific route associations).
- Add a lightweight lifecycle manager module with idempotent create/cleanup primitives and TTL tagging enforcement.
- Replace direct references from long-lived modules with stable outputs and a small interface (resource handles + lookup data) so long-lived state doesn't need every ephemeral id.
- Add an adoption migration path: a one-off migration run and a small compatibility shim so both states can co-exist during cutover.
- Update CI to run plan/apply on long-lived stacks with a reduced drift-detection policy; run transient-state reconciliation more frequently but in isolated pipelines.

Non-goals: complete rewrite of all networking modules, changing VPC topology, or removing existing provider pinning. Provider upgrades can be done in a follow-up once plan churn is reduced.

Success criteria:
- Median terraform plan time for long-lived networking stacks decreases by >=50% in perf tests.
- Number of plan collisions observed in infra CI drops to zero in a 30-day window after cutover.
- No customer-facing incidents caused by the migration; drill via blue/green apply for one region before rolling out globally.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Increased operational complexity: two states vs one. Mitigation: run an operator-mode Terraform module that reconciles cross-state invariants on a scheduled basis and alerts on failures.
- Possible temporary windows where lookups might not find ephemeral resources during cutover. Mitigation: compatibility shim, feature flag gating, and staged rollout by environment.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design doc & diagram (link below) — complete.
2) Prototype transient-state module in staging and run replay tests against recorded infra changes.
3) Implement lookup interface and shim in long-lived modules.
4) Create migration job and CI changes to split state via remote-state export/import with verification.
5) Canary in us-west-2 with test workloads; monitor plan durations and CI collisions.
6) Roll out to other regions and add runbook entries.

comments: 2026-02-03: Kickoff meeting w/ networking, infra CI, and platform teams. Agreed to prototype approach and scoped to EIP/ENI/NAT ephemeral lifecycles.
2026-02-11: Design doc iterated after review from Security (KMS impact) — confirmed no change to KMS usage for long-lived resources.
2026-02-25: Prototype module pushed — initial integration tests pass in isolated staging; observed ~3x faster plan on long-lived stack in synthetic tests.

2026-03-05: Found race during migration where transient-state controller attempted to destroy an ENI before the instance moved. Added ordered reconciliation and finalizers in prototype. See PR #1184 for details.
2026-03-12: Started canary in us-west-2 with infra-canary pipeline. Early metrics: long-lived plan latency reduced from median 9m to 3m 40s. CI collisions went from 5/week down to 1 in first 72h.
2026-03-12: Next steps: finalize runbook, extend test coverage to cross-account VPC peering cases, and schedule a security review for the migration job.
